'''Peter B. Shalen''' (born {{Circa}} 1946) is an American [[mathematician]], working primarily in [[low-dimensional topology]]. He is the "S" in [[JSJ decomposition]].

==Life==
He graduated from [[Stuyvesant High School]] in 1962,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://65.104.11.121/MathTeam.html |title=Stuyvesant Math Team |accessdate=2007-10-31 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001031823/http://65.104.11.121/MathTeam.html |archivedate=2007-10-01 }}</ref> before earning a BA from [[Harvard College]] in 1966 and his PhD from [[Harvard University]] in 1972.<ref>[https://www.math.uic.edu/~shalen/shortvita.pdf Curriculum Vitæ of Peter B. Shalen] Retrieved 9 November 2010</ref> Following academic appointments at [[Columbia University]], [[Rice University]], and the [[Courant Institute|Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], he joined the faculty of the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]].

Shalen was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Foundation Research Fellow]] in mathematics (1977–1979).<ref>[http://www.sloan.org/fellowships/list/s/page/25 Sloan Research Fellowships]{{dead link|date=March 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 1986 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berkeley, California]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Shalen, P. B.|year=1986|chapter=Representations of 3-manifold groups and applications in topology|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, August 3–11, 1986, Berkeley, California|volume=1|pages=607–614}}</ref> He was elected as a member of the 2017 class of [[Fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to three-dimensional topology and for exposition".<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2017 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], [[American Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2016-11-06.</ref>

==Work==
His work with [[Marc Culler]] related properties of representation varieties of [[Hyperbolic manifold|hyperbolic]] [[3-manifold]] [[fundamental group|groups]] to decompositions of 3-manifolds. Based on this work, Culler, [[Cameron Gordon (mathematician)|Cameron Gordon]], [[John Edwin Luecke|John Luecke]], and Shalen proved the [[cyclic surgery theorem]]. An important corollary of the theorem is that at most one nontrivial [[Dehn surgery]] (+1 or −1) on a [[Knot (mathematics)|knot]] can result in a [[Simply connected space|simply-connected]] 3-manifold. This was an important piece of the [[Gordon–Luecke theorem]] that knots are determined by their complements. This paper is often referred to as "CGLS".

With [[John Morgan (mathematician)|John Morgan]], he generalized his work with Culler, and reproved several foundational results of [[William Thurston]].

==Selected publications==
*{{cite book |author1=Jaco, William H. |author2=Shalen, Peter B. |name-list-style=amp | title=Seifert fibered spaces in 3-manifolds | location=Providence | publisher=American Mathematical Society | year=1979 | isbn=0-8218-2220-9}}
*Shalen, Peter B. ''Separating, incompressible surfaces in 3-manifolds.'' [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 52 (1979), no. 2, 105–126.
* Culler, Marc; Shalen, Peter B. ''Varieties of group representations and splittings of 3-manifolds.'' [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2) 117 (1983), no. 1, 109–146.
* Culler, Marc; Gordon, C. McA.; Luecke, J.; Shalen, Peter B. ''Dehn surgery on knots.'' [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2) 125 (1987), no. 2, 237–300.
* Morgan, John W.; Shalen, Peter B. ''Valuations, trees, and degenerations of hyperbolic structures. I.'' Ann. of Math. (2) 120 (1984), no. 3, 401–476.
* Morgan, John W.; Shalen, Peter B. ''Degenerations of hyperbolic structures. II. Measured laminations in 3-manifolds.'' [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2) 127 (1988), no. 2, 403–456.
* Morgan, John W.; Shalen, Peter B. ''Degenerations of hyperbolic structures. III. Actions of 3-manifold groups on trees and Thurston's compactness theorem.'' [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2) 127 (1988), no. 3, 457–519.
